ESV.1: An oracle concerning Moab. Because Ar of Moab is laid waste in a night, Moab is undone; because Kir of Moab is laid waste in a night, Moab is undone.
ESV.2: He has gone up to the temple,  and to Dibon, to the high places  to weep; over Nebo and over Medeba Moab wails. On every head is baldness; every beard is shorn;
ESV.3: in the streets they wear sackcloth; on the housetops and in the squares everyone wails and melts in tears.
ESV.4: Heshbon and Elealeh cry out; their voice is heard as far as Jahaz; therefore the armed men of Moab cry aloud; his soul trembles.
ESV.5: My heart cries out for Moab; her fugitives flee to Zoar, to Eglath-shelishiyah. For at the ascent of Luhith they go up weeping; on the road to Horonaim they raise a cry of destruction;
ESV.6: the waters of Nimrim are a desolation; the grass is withered, the vegetation fails, the greenery is no more.
ESV.7: Therefore the abundance they have gained and what they have laid up they carry away over the Brook of the Willows.
ESV.8: For a cry has gone around the land of Moab; her wailing reaches to Eglaim; her wailing reaches to Beer-elim.
ESV.9: For the waters of Dibon  are full of blood; for I will bring upon Dibon even more, a lion for those of Moab who escape, for the remnant of the land.

NASB.1: The oracle concerning Moab. Surely in a night Ar of Moab is devastated [and] ruined; Surely in a night Kir of Moab is devastated [and] ruined.
NASB.2: They have gone up to the temple and [to] Dibon, [even] to the high places to weep. Moab wails over Nebo and Medeba; Everyone's head is bald [and] every beard is cut off.
NASB.3: In their streets they have girded themselves with sackcloth; On their housetops and in their squares Everyone is wailing, dissolved in tears.
NASB.4: Heshbon and Elealeh also cry out, Their voice is heard all the way to Jahaz; Therefore the armed men of Moab cry aloud; His soul trembles within him.
NASB.5: My heart cries out for Moab; His fugitives are as far as Zoar [and] Eglath-shelishiyah, For they go up the ascent of Luhith weeping; Surely on the road to Horonaim they raise a cry of distress over [their] ruin.
NASB.6: For the waters of Nimrim are desolate. Surely the grass is withered, the tender grass died out, There is no green thing.
NASB.7: Therefore the abundance [which] they have acquired and stored up They carry off over the brook of Arabim.
NASB.8: For the cry of distress has gone around the territory of Moab, Its wail [goes] as far as Eglaim and its wailing even to Beer-elim.
NASB.9: For the waters of Dimon are full of blood; Surely I will bring added [woes] upon Dimon, A lion upon the fugitives of Moab and upon the remnant of the land.

NKJV.1: The burden against Moab. Because in the night Ar of Moab is laid waste And destroyed, Because in the night Kir of Moab is laid waste And destroyed,
NKJV.2: He has gone up to the temple and Dibon, To the high places to weep. Moab will wail over Nebo and over Medeba; On all their heads will be baldness, And every beard cut off.
NKJV.3: In their streets they will clothe themselves with sackcloth; On the tops of their houses And in their streets Everyone will wail, weeping bitterly.
NKJV.4: Heshbon and Elealeh will cry out, Their voice shall be heard as far as Jahaz; Therefore the armed soldiers of Moab will cry out; His life will be burdensome to him.
NKJV.5: “My heart will cry out for Moab; His fugitives shall flee to Zoar, Like a three-year-old heifer. For by the Ascent of Luhith They will go up with weeping; For in the way of Horonaim They will raise up a cry of destruction,
NKJV.6: For the waters of Nimrim will be desolate, For the green grass has withered away; The grass fails, there is nothing green.
NKJV.7: Therefore the abundance they have gained, And what they have laid up, They will carry away to the Brook of the Willows.
NKJV.8: For the cry has gone all around the borders of Moab, Its wailing to Eglaim And its wailing to Beer Elim.
NKJV.9: For the waters of Dimon will be full of blood; Because I will bring more upon Dimon,  Lions upon him who escapes from Moab, And on the remnant of the land.”

NLT.1:
This message came to me concerning Moab: In one night the town of Ar will be leveled,
and the city of Kir will be destroyed.
NLT.2:
Your people will go to their temple in Dibon to mourn.
They will go to their sacred shrines to weep.
They will wail for the fate of Nebo and Medeba,
shaving their heads in sorrow and cutting off their beards.
NLT.3:
They will wear burlap as they wander the streets.
From every home and public square will come the sound of wailing.
NLT.4:
The people of Heshbon and Elealeh will cry out;
their voices will be heard as far away as Jahaz!
The bravest warriors of Moab will cry out in utter terror.
They will be helpless with fear.
NLT.5:
My heart weeps for Moab.
Its people flee to Zoar and Eglath-shelishiyah.
Weeping, they climb the road to Luhith.
Their cries of distress can be heard all along the road to Horonaim.
NLT.6:
Even the waters of Nimrim are dried up!
The grassy banks are scorched.
The tender plants are gone;
nothing green remains.
NLT.7:
The people grab their possessions
and carry them across the Ravine of Willows.
NLT.8:
A cry of distress echoes through the land of Moab
from one end to the other —
from Eglaim to Beer-elim.
NLT.9:
The stream near Dibon runs red with blood,
but I am still not finished with Dibon!
Lions will hunt down the survivors —
both those who try to escape
and those who remain behind.

WEB.1: The burden of Moab: for in a night, Ar of Moab is laid waste, and brought to nothing; for in a night Kir of Moab is laid waste, and brought to nothing.
WEB.2: They have gone up to Bayith, and to Dibon, to the high places, to weep. Moab wails over Nebo and over Medeba. Baldness is on all of their heads. Every beard is cut off.
WEB.3: In their streets, they clothe themselves in sackcloth. In their streets and on their housetops, everyone wails, weeping abundantly.
WEB.4: Heshbon cries out with Elealeh. Their voice is heard even to Jahaz. Therefore the armed men of Moab cry aloud. Their souls tremble within them.
WEB.5: My heart cries out for Moab! Her nobles flee to Zoar, to Eglath Shelishiyah; for they go up by the ascent of Luhith with weeping; for on the way to Horonaim, they raise up a cry of destruction.
WEB.6: For the waters of Nimrim will be desolate; for the grass has withered away, the tender grass fails, there is no green thing.
WEB.7: Therefore they will carry away the abundance they have gotten, and that which they have stored up, over the brook of the willows.
WEB.8: For the cry has gone around the borders of Moab; its wailing to Eglaim, and its wailing to Beer Elim.
WEB.9: For the waters of Dimon are full of blood; for I will bring yet more on Dimon, a lion on those of Moab who escape, and on the remnant of the land.

AMP.1:
The [mournful, inspired] oracle ( a burden to be carried) concerning Moab:
Because in a night Ar of Moab is devastated and ruined;
Because in a night Kir of Moab is devastated and ruined.
AMP.2:
They have gone up to the temple and to Dibon, to the high places to weep.
Moab wails over Nebo and over Medeba;
Everyone's head is shaved, and every beard is cut off [in mourning].
AMP.3:
In their streets they have wrapped themselves with sackcloth;
On their [flat] housetops and in their open squares
Everyone is wailing, dissolved in tears.
AMP.4:
Heshbon and Elealeh [cities claimed by Moab] cry out;
Their voice is heard as far as Jahaz.
Therefore the armed men of Moab cry out;
Moab's soul trembles within him.
AMP.5:
My heart cries out for Moab;
His fugitives are [fleeing] as far as Zoar and Eglath-shelishiyah.
For they go up the ascent of Luhith weeping;
For on the road to Horonaim they raise a cry of distress over their destruction.
AMP.6:
For the waters of Nimrim are desolate.
Indeed the grass is withered, the new growth dies;
There is no green thing.
AMP.7:
Therefore the abundance which they have acquired and stored away
They carry off over the Brook of the Willows.
AMP.8:
For the cry of distress has echoed around the territory of Moab;
The wailing goes as far as Eglaim and the mournful cry to Beer-elim.
AMP.9:
For the waters of Dimon are full of blood;
Yet I will bring even more woes on Dimon—
A lion upon those of Moab who escape and upon the remnant of the land.

MSG.1:
A Message concerning Moab:
Village Ar of Moab is in ruins,
destroyed in a night raid.
Village Kir of Moab is in ruins,
destroyed in a night raid.
MSG.2:
Village Dibon climbs to its chapel in the hills,
goes up to lament.
Moab weeps and wails
over Nebo and Medba.
Every head is shaved bald,
every beard shaved clean.
MSG.3:
They pour into the streets wearing black,
go up on the roofs, take to the town square,
Everyone in tears,
everyone in grief.
MSG.4:
Towns Heshbon and Elealeh cry long and loud.
The sound carries as far as Jahaz.
Moab sobs, shaking in grief.
The soul of Moab trembles.
MSG.5:
Oh, how I grieve for Moab!
Refugees stream to Zoar
and then on to Eglath-shelishiyah.
Up the slopes of Luhith they weep;
on the road to Horonaim they cry their loss.
MSG.6:
The springs of Nimrim are dried up—
grass brown, buds stunted, nothing grows.
MSG.7:
They leave, carrying all their possessions
on their backs, everything they own,
Making their way as best they can
across Willow Creek to safety.
MSG.8:
Poignant cries reverberate
all through Moab,
Gut-wrenching sobs as far as Eglaim,
heart-racking sobs all the way to Beer-elim.
MSG.9:
The banks of the Dibon crest with blood,
but God has worse in store for Dibon:
A lion—a lion to finish off the fugitives,
to clean up whoever's left in the land.

NIV.1:
A Prophecy Against Moab
An oracle concerning Moab:
Ar in Moab is ruined,
destroyed in a night!
Kir in Moab is ruined,
destroyed in a night!
NIV.2:
Dibon goes up to its temple,
to its high places to weep;
Moab wails over Nebo and Medeba.
Every head is shaved
and every beard cut off.
NIV.3:
In the streets they wear sackcloth;
on the roofs and in the public squares
they all wail,
prostrate with weeping.
NIV.4:
Heshbon and Elealeh cry out,
their voices are heard all the way to Jahaz.
Therefore the armed men of Moab cry out,
and their hearts are faint.
NIV.5:
My heart cries out over Moab;
her fugitives flee as far as Zoar,
as far as Eglath Shelishiyah.
They go up the way to Luhith,
weeping as they go;
on the road to Horonaim
they lament their destruction.
NIV.6:
The waters of Nimrim are dried up
and the grass is withered;
the vegetation is gone
and nothing green is left.
NIV.7:
So the wealth they have acquired and stored up
they carry away over the Ravine of the Poplars.
NIV.8:
Their outcry echoes along the border of Moab;
their wailing reaches as far as Eglaim,
their lamentation as far as Beer Elim.
NIV.9:
Dimon’s waters are full of blood,
but I will bring still more upon Dimon—
a lion upon the fugitives of Moab
and upon those who remain in the land.

NET.1: Here is a message about Moab: Indeed, in a night it is devastated, Ar of Moab is destroyed! Indeed, in a night it is devastated, Kir of Moab is destroyed!
NET.2: They went up to the temple, the people of Dibon went up to the high places to lament. Because of what happened to Nebo and Medeba, Moab wails. Every head is shaved bare, every beard is trimmed off.
NET.3: In their streets they wear sackcloth; on their roofs and in their town squares all of them wail, they fall down weeping.
NET.4: The people of Heshbon and Elealeh cry out, their voices are heard as far away as Jahaz. For this reason Moab’s soldiers shout in distress; their courage wavers.
NET.5: My heart cries out because of Moab’s plight, and for the fugitives stretched out as far as Zoar and Eglath Shelishiyah. For they weep as they make their way up the ascent of Luhith; they loudly lament their demise on the road to Horonaim.
NET.6: For the waters of Nimrim are gone; the grass is dried up, the vegetation has disappeared, and there are no plants.
NET.7: For this reason what they have made and stored up, they carry over the Stream of the Poplars.
NET.8: Indeed, the cries of distress echo throughout Moabite territory; their wailing can be heard in Eglaim and Beer Elim.
NET.9: Indeed, the waters of Dimon are full of blood! Indeed, I will heap even more trouble on Dimon. A lion will attack the Moabite fugitives and the people left in the land.
